title: This OpEx Week Is About To Get Wild
speaker: Geeks of Finance host

macro_themes.view: OpEx weeks have a historically positive bias; call buying at 7850/7900 skews GEX upside for the week.
VIX in a downtrend since April, capped by negative gamma at the 15-16 strikes.
Bitcoin and AI-infrastructure names in uptrends act as leading indicators for further market drift higher.

calls.reason: Largest gamma at 7800, upside skew to 7900, call buying at 7850/7900; 8000 gamma magnet with price channelling toward it; short 7825 puts.
calls.quote: a move up towards 8,000 before year end has a pretty decent probability

calls.reason: Negative gamma at 15/16 strikes caps volatility; downtrend since April.
calls.quote: it's really capping the volatility index out at these levels

calls.reason: Trading low 80,000s, pulled back into steeply rising 10/20/50-day MAs; gamma concentrations at 90k and 95k.
calls.quote: making its way towards these higher gamma exposure concentrations at the 90 and 95,000 strikes

calls.condition: Looking for a tag of 600 (gamma level + 20-day SMA) as a bounce zone
calls.reason: Pulled back four sessions into strongly negative GEX but still above 20 SMA and 50 EMA; 600 bounce zone.
calls.quote: getting down to that 600 level could provide a big bounce opportunity

calls.condition: Looking for a bounce back above 1050 this week; possible gamma squeeze exiting negative GEX
calls.reason: Uptrend since July from 800, stacked rising MAs, most GEX at 1000 and above; short 1050/long 1040 put spread.
calls.quote: we're looking for a little bit of a bounce back above that 1050 level this week

calls.reason: Breaking out of six-week 130-140 consolidation; big gamma at 150 strike; short 135/133 put spread expiring Friday.
calls.quote: We think that 150 level is likely to get hit

notes: Recorded over the weekend after Fri Oct 9 close (S&P 7811.51, VIX 14.79); no explicit date stated, listing date Oct 12 used. Micron GEX range transcribed garbled ('1,00 and,00'), recorded only as 1000+. ServiceNow 'up 81%' is a transcription error (likely 0.81%). S&P 7825 refers to their short put strike.
